issues.claim: the Scrum Guide makes the Product Owner accountable for backlog items being understood (RU: "возлагает на Product Owner ответственность за то, чтобы элементы бэклога были понятны")
issues.problem: The fetched Scrum Guide excerpt is cut off before the Product Owner section, so it does not show this claim. I recall the 2020 Scrum Guide saying the Product Owner is accountable for "ensuring that the Product Backlog is transparent, visible and understood", but I cannot confirm that from the excerpt. The wording is also slightly narrower in the question: the Guide says the Product Backlog is understood, not each item. The Agile Manifesto principle ("Business people and developers must work together daily throughout the project") is confirmed by the excerpt.
issues.suggestedFix: Confirm the Product Owner wording on the live page. Or soften it to: "the Scrum Guide makes the Product Owner accountable for the Product Backlog being transparent, visible and understood" (RU: "...чтобы Product Backlog был прозрачным, видимым и понятным"). Keep the same wording in both locales.

issues.claim: Кто на самом деле знает правильное толкование и как убедиться, что вы с ним поняли задачу одинаково?
issues.problem: The hint is acceptable and does not give away the whole answer, but it points directly at "ask the owner and confirm", which is the core of the answer. It is slightly strong for a junior open question.
issues.suggestedFix: Optional: make it a little more neutral, for example "Как снизить цену ошибки, если вы выберете не то толкование, до того как написан код?" Make the same change in the English hint.

issues.claim: Deliberate debt is acceptable when it is visible and has a plan to pay it back. Skipping tests with no record and no date is reckless debt.
issues.problem: This is presented as Fowler's quadrant, but the quadrant is about design debt, not tests. The page says that going "quick and dirty" because the team thinks it cannot afford the time for clean code is usually reckless debt, because people underestimate the DesignPayoffLine. That is exactly the "skip tests to hit Friday" case. The explanation therefore teaches a candidate that Fowler blesses this shortcut as prudent, which is misleading. Fowler's prudent-deliberate example is a conscious weighing of the payoff of an earlier release against the cost of paying the debt. The visible-and-planned criterion is the author's own view, not Fowler's.
issues.suggestedFix: Rewrite the paragraph in both locales, for example: "Fowler's quadrant separates deliberate-prudent debt (a conscious decision that the payoff of releasing earlier exceeds the cost of repaying the debt) from reckless debt. He warns that cutting corners because 'we have no time for clean code' is usually reckless, because people underestimate how soon quality pays off. That is why the first move is to cut scope. If the shortcut is still chosen, making it explicit, recorded and time-boxed is the way to keep it closer to the prudent end." Attribute the recording and payback practice to good practice, not to Fowler.

issues.claim: we must ship now and deal with the consequences (Deliberate/Prudent cell)
issues.problem: The cell text lives in the quadrant diagram on the page. The fetched excerpt only contains prose and does not show the quote. I recall this being the correct prudent/deliberate label, but I cannot confirm it from the excerpt.
issues.suggestedFix: Confirm the diagram wording on the live page. If unsure, paraphrase without quotation marks: "a deliberate, prudent decision to ship now and deal with the consequences later".

issues.claim: high internal quality does not slow development down but speeds it up: accumulated problems in the code start to slow work fairly soon
issues.problem: The excerpt supports the thesis that high-quality software is cheaper to produce and that the quality/cost trade-off does not apply. It is cut off before the part about how soon cruft starts to hurt, so "fairly soon" is not shown. From memory the article puts this at weeks rather than months, but that is not in the excerpt.
issues.suggestedFix: Either confirm the timing on the page, or reword without a time frame: "Fowler argues that high internal quality makes software cheaper to produce, because accumulated cruft slows the team down." Make the same change in the RU text.
